questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Law Commission of India is correct?
o: It is a permanent department under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
It is a constitutional body established under Article 280.
It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
It is a non-statutory advisory body.
questions.e: The Law Commission of India is a non-statutory advisory body. It is established by the order of the Central Government from time to time for a fixed tenure.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the first Law Commission established in independent India?
questions.e: The first Law Commission of independent India was established in 1955 for a three-year term. It was headed by M.C. Setalvad, who was the then Attorney-General of India.

questions.q: Which British-era official served as the Chairman of the First Law Commission established in 1834?
questions.e: During the British regime, four Law Commissions were established in the 19th century. The First Law Commission was established in 1834 and was headed by Lord Macaulay.

questions.q: What is the standard tenure for a Law Commission of India?
questions.e: The Law Commission is established by the order of the Central Government for a fixed tenure. Since 1955, Law Commissions have generally been constituted with a three-year term.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Law Commission of India?
o: To provide research to foreign countries if referred by the Government.
To issue binding orders to the Supreme Court.
To examine existing laws in light of Directive Principles.
To identify laws that can be immediately repealed.
questions.e: The function of the Law Commission is to recommend legislative measures for consolidation and codification of laws. However, its recommendations are not binding on the government.

questions.q: Who generally serves as the Member-Secretary of the Law Commission of India?
o: A retired Chief Justice of India
A Professor of Law from a National Law University
An eminent member of the Bar
An officer of the Indian Legal Service holding the rank of Secretary or Additional Secretary
questions.e: The composition of the Commission varies. Generally, the Member-Secretary belongs to the Indian Legal Service and holds the rank of either Additional Secretary or Secretary to the Government of India.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment gave constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies?
questions.e: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 gave constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies. It made the right to form co-operative societies a fundamental right under Article 19.

questions.q: Under the 97th Amendment Act, what is the maximum number of directors allowed for a co-operative society?
questions.e: According to Part IX-B of the Constitution, the board of a co-operative society shall consist of such number of directors as provided by the state legislature. However, the maximum number of directors shall not exceed twenty-one.

questions.q: Which Part of the Constitution was added by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011?
questions.e: The 97th Amendment Act added a new Part IX-B to the Constitution, entitled "The Co-operative Societies," covering Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT.

questions.q: What is the fixed term of office for elected members of the board of a co-operative society?
questions.e: The term of office of elected members of the board and its office bearers shall be five years from the date of election.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding co-operative society boards — 1️⃣ Reservation of one seat for SCs/STs 2️⃣ Reservation of two seats for women 3️⃣ Co-option of up to two members with banking or finance experience
questions.e: State legislatures must provide for reservation of one seat for SC/STs and two seats for women on the board of every co-operative society having such members. The legislature also provides for co-option of up to two members with experience in banking, management, or finance.

questions.q: A co-operative society board cannot be superseded or kept under suspension for a period exceeding:
questions.e: No board shall be superseded or kept under suspension for a period exceeding six months. However, for co-operative banks (other than multi-state), this period can be up to one year.

questions.q: In the 2021 judgment (Union of India vs. Rajendra Shah), the Supreme Court held that Part IX-B of the Constitution is operative only for:
questions.e: In 2021, the Supreme Court upheld a Gujarat High Court judgment striking down Part IX-B except as it concerns multi-state co-operative societies both within states and union territories.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the Official Language of the Union?
questions.e: Part XVII of the Constitution deals with the official language in Articles 343 to 351. Article 343 specifically deals with the Official language of the Union.

questions.q: According to the Constitution, what is the official language of the Union?
o: Any language listed in the Eighth Schedule
Hindi in Devanagari script and English
questions.e: Hindi written in Devanagari script is to be the official language of the Union. However, the form of numerals to be used is the international form of Indian numerals.

questions.q: For how many years from the commencement of the Constitution was English to continue for all official purposes of the Union?
questions.e: The Constitution provided that for a period of fifteen years from its commencement (1950 to 1965), English would continue to be used for all official purposes of the Union.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the first Official Language Commission appointed in 1955?
questions.e: In 1955, the President appointed an Official Language Commission under the chairmanship of B.G. Kher.

questions.q: Which Act provides for the continued use of English indefinitely for official purposes of the Union?
questions.e: The Parliament enacted the Official Languages Act in 1963, which provides for the continued use of English (even after 1965) in addition to Hindi for all official purposes of the Union and transaction of business in Parliament. This Act enables the use of English indefinitely.

questions.q: Which authority can authorize the use of Hindi or any other official language in the proceedings of a High Court?
o: The Governor of the state, with previous consent of the President
The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The Governor of a state, with the previous consent of the President, can authorize the use of Hindi or any other official language of the state in the proceedings of the High Court.

questions.q: Judgments, decrees, and orders of a High Court must be in which language unless Parliament provides otherwise?
questions.e: Until Parliament provides otherwise, all proceedings in the Supreme Court and every High Court, including judgments, decrees, and orders, must be in English.

questions.q: Which Article directs the State to provide facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education for linguistic minorities?
questions.e: Article 350A directs that every state and local authority should provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education for children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

questions.q: How many languages are currently specified in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.e: At present, the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution specifies 22 languages. Originally, it contained 14 languages.

questions.q: Which was the first language to be granted 'Classical Language' status in India?
questions.e: In 2004, the Government created the "classical languages" category. Tamil was the first language declared a classical language in 2004.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a criteria for determining 'Classical Language' status?
o: High antiquity of early texts (1500-2000 years).
The language must be spoken by at least 10% of the population.
A body of ancient literature considered a valuable heritage.
questions.e: The criteria include high antiquity of texts over 1500-2000 years, a body of ancient literature, and an original literary tradition . Population percentage is not a criterion.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Father of All-India Services'?
questions.e: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the chief protagonist of All-India Services in the Constituent Assembly, and hence he is regarded as the 'Father of All-India Services'.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution authorizes the Parliament to create new All-India Services?
questions.e: Article 312 of the Constitution authorizes the Parliament of India to create new All-India Services based on a resolution passed by Rajya Sabha to that effect.

questions.q: A resolution to create a new All-India Service in the Rajya Sabha must be supported by:
o: Two-thirds of the members present and voting
questions.e: A resolution in the Rajya Sabha for creating a new All-India service should be supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting.

questions.q: Which Ministry manages and controls the Indian Administrative Service (IAS)?
o: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
questions.e: The IAS is managed and controlled by the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

questions.q: Members of the All-India Services hold office during the "pleasure" of:
questions.e: According to Article 310, members of the defence services, the civil services of the Centre, and the all-India services hold office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.q: Which Article provides safeguards to civil servants against arbitrary dismissal?
questions.e: Article 311 provides two safeguards to civil servants: they cannot be dismissed by an authority subordinate to their appointing authority, and they cannot be dismissed without an inquiry and reasonable opportunity of being heard.

questions.q: In which case is the safeguard of holding an inquiry NOT available to a civil servant?
o: Where the authority is satisfied that it is not reasonably practicable to hold an inquiry.
Where the President/Governor is satisfied that it is not expedient in the interest of state security.
Dismissal on grounds of conduct leading to conviction on a criminal charge.
questions.e: The safeguard of holding an inquiry is not available in three cases: conviction on a criminal charge, lack of practicability (recorded in writing), or in the interest of the security of the state .

questions.q: The Indian Foreign Service (IFS) is classified as a:
questions.e: The Indian Foreign Service is a Group A Central Service. It is the topmost Central Service in terms of prestige and pay.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for the delimitation of constituencies in India?
questions.e: The job of fixing limits or boundaries of territorial constituencies is assigned to a high-powered body known as the Delimitation Commission or Boundary Commission.

questions.q: Orders issued by the Delimitation Commission:
o: Can be challenged in the Supreme Court
Can be modified by the Lok Sabha
Have the force of law and cannot be challenged in any court
Require approval from the State Legislature
questions.e: The Delimitation Commission is a powerful body; its orders have the force of law and cannot be challenged in any court.

questions.q: According to the 84th and 87th Amendment Acts, the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha is frozen until the first census after the year:
questions.e: The cumulative effect of the 84th and 87th Amendment Acts is that the total number of seats in the Lok Sabha as allocated on the basis of the 1971 census shall remain unaltered till the first census taken after the year 2026.

questions.q: Who serves as an ex-officio member of the Delimitation Commission?
questions.e: The Fourth Delimitation Commission (2002) consisted of a Chairperson (retired or serving Supreme Court judge), the Chief Election Commissioner (or an nominee) as an ex-officio member, and the State Election Commissioner of the concerned state as an ex-officio member .

questions.q: The North Eastern Council (NEC) was established in which year?
questions.e: The North Eastern Council is a statutory advisory body established in 1972 through the North Eastern Council Act, 1971.

questions.q: Which state became the eighth member state of the North Eastern Council in 2002?
questions.e: The Council originally consisted of seven states. In 2002, Sikkim became the eighth member state of the Council.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the North Eastern Council since July 2018?
questions.e: Since July 2018, the Union Home Minister is the ex-officio Chairman and the Minister (In-charge) of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DONER) is the ex-officio Vice-Chairman.

questions.q: Which Article states that the Government of India may sue or be sued by the name of the Union of India?
questions.e: Article 300 of the Constitution lays down that the Government of India may sue or be sued by the name of the Union of India.

questions.q: Under Article 299, contracts made in the exercise of executive power of the Union must be executed on behalf of:
questions.e: Contracts must be expressed to be made by the President (for the Union) or Governor (for a state) and must be executed on their behalf.

questions.q: The traditional immunity of the State for tortious acts of its servants was reaffirm in 1964 in which case?
o: P and O Steam Navigation Company case
questions.e: The immunity of the government in respect of its sovereign functions was established in the P and O Steam Navigation Company case (1861) and reaffirmed by the Supreme Court in the Kasturilal case (1964).

questions.q: In which 1994 case did the Supreme Court rule that the State cannot avoid liability for damages caused by negligent acts of its servants on the ground of sovereign immunity?
questions.e: In the Nagendra Rao case (1994), the Supreme Court adopted a liberal approach, ruling that the State is liable to pay compensation for damages due to the negligent act of its servants and cannot avoid liability on the ground of sovereign immunity.

questions.q: What is the legal requirement before starting civil proceedings against the President or a Governor for personal acts during their term?
o: Consent of the Council of Ministers
questions.e: Civil proceedings can be started against the President or Governors during their term of office in respect of personal acts only after giving two months' advance notice.

questions.q: Part XVI of the Constitution (Articles 330 to 342A) contains special provisions for:
o: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Backward Classes, and Anglo-Indians
questions.e: Part XVI of the Constitution, from Articles 330 to 342A, makes special provisions for scheduled castes (SCs), scheduled tribes (STs), backward classes (BCs), and Anglo-Indians.

questions.q: Who has the power to specify which castes or tribes shall be treated as SCs or STs in a State?
questions.e: The Constitution leaves to the President the power to specify what castes or tribes in each state and union territory are to be treated as SCs and STs. In the case of states, this is done after consulting the governor.

questions.q: Inclusion or exclusion of a caste from the Presidential notification regarding SCs/STs can be done only by:
questions.e: Any inclusion or exclusion of any caste or tribe from the Presidential notification can be done only by the Parliament and not by a subsequent Presidential notification.

questions.q: Under the 104th Amendment Act of 2019, reservation for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha is extended until:
questions.e: Originally intended for ten years, the reservation duration has been extended every ten years. Under the 104th Amendment Act of 2019, reservation is to last until 2030 .

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate bodies?
questions.e: Previously, there was a combined commission. The 89th Amendment Act of 2003 bifurcated it into the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (Article 338) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338-A).

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the first Backward Classes Commission appointed in 1953?
questions.e: The first backward classes commission was appointed in 1953 under the chairmanship of Kaka Kalelkar.

questions.q: The provision for nominating two members of the Anglo-Indian community to the Lok Sabha ceased to have effect on:
questions.e: The 104th Amendment Act, 2019, did not extend the provision for special representation of Anglo-Indians by nomination. Consequently, it ceased to have effect on 25th January 2020 .

questions.q: Article 371-A provides special provisions for which state?
questions.e: Article 371-A makes special provisions for the state of Nagaland.

questions.q: Under Article 371-F, the Sikkim Legislative Assembly must consist of at least:
questions.e: The 36th Amendment Act (1975) made Sikkim a full-fledged state and included Article 371-F, which stipulates the Sikkim Legislative Assembly shall consist of not less than 30 members .

questions.q: Article 371-J, providing special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, was inserted by which amendment?
questions.e: Article 371-J, which provides for special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region of Karnataka, was inserted by the 98th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2012.

questions.q: Which type of political parties cling to old socio-economic and political institutions?
questions.e: Reactionary parties cling to the old socio-economic and political institutions.

questions.q: Political parties that aim at establishing a new order by overthrowing existing institutions are called:
questions.e: Radical parties aim at establishing a new order by overthrowing the existing institutions.

questions.q: Who referred to the Indian party system as the 'one party dominance system' or the 'Congress system'?
questions.e: Rajni Kothari, an eminent political analyst, preferred to call the Indian party system the 'one party dominance system' or the 'Congress system'.

questions.q: At present, a party is recognized as a National Party if it wins what percentage of seats in the Lok Sabha from at least three states?
questions.e: One condition for recognition as a national party is if it wins two per cent of seats in the Lok Sabha at a general election, and these candidates are elected from three states.

questions.q: A party is recognized as a State Party if it wins at least how many seats in the Legislative Assembly of the state concerned?
questions.e: A party is recognized as a state party if it secures six per cent of valid votes in a general election to the state assembly and, in addition, wins 2 seats in that assembly.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a regional party?
o: It aims to capture political power at the national level.
Its electoral base is limited to a single region.
It operates within a particular state.
questions.e: Features of regional parties include operating within a particular state, limited electoral base, and aiming to capture power at the state level .

questions.q: Which Article vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission of India?
questions.e: The Constitution (Article 324) provides for an independent Election Commission and vests in it the power of superintendence, direction, and conduct of elections to Parliament, state legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.q: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 years to:
questions.e: The 61st Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years. This came into force in March 1989.

questions.q: Election petitions are triable by which authority?
questions.e: Since 1966, election petitions are triable by High Courts alone. However, the appellate jurisdiction lies with the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Who designates the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of a State?
o: The Election Commission of India in consultation with the State Government
questions.e: The Election Commission of India nominates or designates an officer of the State Government as the Chief Electoral Officer in consultation with that State Government.

questions.q: Which officer is responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls for a constituency?
questions.e: The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) is responsible for the preparation of electoral rolls for a Parliamentary/assembly constituency.

questions.q: The Model Code of Conduct comes into effect immediately after:
o: The Election Commission announces the schedule of elections
The President dissolves the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The Model Code of Conduct for guidance of candidates and political parties comes immediately into effect after the announcement of the election schedule by the Election Commission.

questions.q: What is the minimum campaign period officially allowed from the drawing up of the list of nominated candidates?
questions.e: The official campaign lasts at least two weeks from the drawing up of the list of nominated candidates.

questions.q: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were used for the first time in the entire state for general elections in:
questions.e: EVMs were used for the first time on an experimental basis in 1998. They were used for the first time in general elections for an entire state in the Assembly elections of Goa in 1999.

questions.q: Election petitions are NOT ordinary civil suits but are treated as:
o: Contests in which the whole constituency is involved
questions.e: An election petition is not an ordinary civil suit but is treated as a contest in which the whole constituency is involved.

questions.q: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 primarily deals with:
o: Allocation of seats and registration of electors
questions.e: The Representation of the People Act, 1950 was enacted to provide for the allocation of seats in legislatures and the registration of electors for constituencies.

questions.q: Which Act contains provisions for the actual conduct of elections and the registration of political parties?
questions.e: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 contains provisions for the actual conduct of elections, qualifications/disqualifications for membership, corrupt practices, and registration of political parties.

questions.q: Which committee recommended the introduction of state funding of elections?
questions.e: In 1998, the Indrajit Gupta Committee on state funding of elections was appointed. It submitted its report in 1999, upholding the argument for state funding as legally justified and in the public interest.

questions.q: Under the 1996 electoral reforms, a candidate is restricted from contesting from more than how many constituencies?
questions.e: As per the 1996 reforms, a candidate is not eligible to contest from more than two Parliamentary or assembly constituencies at a general election or simultaneous by-elections.

questions.q: In 2003, which system was introduced for elections to the Rajya Sabha to curb cross-voting?
questions.e: In 2003, an open ballot system was introduced for Rajya Sabha elections to curb cross-voting and the role of money power.

questions.q: Since which year has the NOTA (None of the Above) option been provided in General Elections?
questions.e: The provision for NOTA has been made since the General Elections to State Legislative Assemblies in 2013.

questions.q: What does VVPAT stand for?
o: Voter Verification and Paper Audit Trail
questions.e: VVPAT stands for Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail, an independent system that allows voters to verify their votes are cast as intended.

questions.q: According to the 2017 budget, the limit for anonymous cash donations to a political party was lowered from ₹20,000 to:
questions.e: In the 2017 budget, the limit for anonymous cash donations by an individual to a political party was lowered from ₹20,000 to ₹2,000.

questions.q: Which reform was introduced by the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021?
o: Linking of electoral roll data with Aadhaar ecosystem
questions.e: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 enabled the linking of electoral roll data with the Aadhaar ecosystem to curb multiple enrolments.

questions.q: The term used for the scientific study of voting behaviour is:
questions.e: Psephology, a branch of political science, deals with the scientific study of voting behaviour.

questions.q: Which eminent political analyst stated that "Indian politics is casteist, and caste is politicised"?
questions.e: Rajni Kothari, an eminent political analyst, stated that "Indian politics is casteist, and caste is politicised," highlighting the influence of caste on voting behaviour.

questions.q: The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 is popularly known as:
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 provided for disqualification of members on the ground of defection and is often referred to as the 'anti-defection law'.

questions.q: Which Schedule was added to the Constitution by the Anti-Defection Law?
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 added a new Schedule, the Tenth Schedule, to the Constitution.

questions.q: An independent member becomes disqualified if they join any political party:
o: Only if they become a Minister
questions.e: An independent member of a House becomes disqualified to remain a member if he/she joins any political party after such election.

questions.q: A nominated member can join a political party without disqualification within:
questions.e: A nominated member becomes disqualified if they join a political party after the expiry of six months from taking their seat; thus, they may join within those six months.

questions.q: Disqualification on ground of defection does NOT apply if a merger takes place with:
questions.e: Disqualification does not apply if a member goes out of his/her party due to a merger, which occurs when two-thirds of the members have agreed.

questions.q: Who is the deciding authority for questions regarding disqualification arising out of defection?
o: The Presiding Officer of the House
questions.e: Any question regarding disqualification arising out of defection is to be decided by the presiding officer of the House.

questions.q: In the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), the Supreme Court ruled that the Presiding Officer's decision under the Tenth Schedule is:
questions.e: In the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), the Supreme Court held that the presiding officer functions as a tribunal and their decision is subject to judicial review on grounds of mala fides or perversity .

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment Act (2003), the total number of ministers in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed:
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 provided that the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: The term 'pressure group' originated in which country?
questions.e: The term 'pressure group' originated in the USA.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an agrarian pressure group in India?
questions.e: The Bhartiya Kisan Union is an agrarian group representing farmers. FICCI is a business group, AITUC is a trade union, and IMA is a professional association.

questions.q: Spontaneous pressure groups like those involved in riots or demonstrations are called:
questions.e: Anomic pressure groups refer to spontaneous breakthroughs into the political system from society, such as riots or demonstrations.

questions.q: Which conference in 1961 led to the setting up of the National Integration Council (NIC)?
questions.e: In 1961, the central government convened the National Integration Conference, which decided to set up the National Integration Council (NIC).

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of the National Integration Council?
questions.e: The NIC consists of the Prime Minister as Chairman, along with Union Ministers and other leaders.

questions.q: In the Romesh Thappar case (1950), the Supreme Court ruled that freedom of speech and expression includes:
questions.e: In the Romesh Thappar case (1950), the Supreme Court held that freedom of speech and expression includes freedom of propagation of ideas, which is ensured by the freedom of circulation.

questions.q: Which landmark case led to the emergence of the 'doctrine of basic structure'?
questions.e: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) led to the emergence of the doctrine of basic structure as a limitation on the amending power of Parliament.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court lay down the 'rarest of rare cases' doctrine for awarding the death penalty?
questions.e: The Bachan Singh case (1980) led to the laying down of the doctrine of 'rarest of rare cases' for awarding the death penalty.

questions.q: Which judgment led to the enactment of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013?
questions.e: The Vishaka case (1997) laid down guidelines known as 'Vishaka Guidelines' which filled the legislative vacuum until the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 was enacted.

questions.q: The doctrine of 'Pith and Substance' is used to:
o: Determine if a law is fundamental
Decide the true nature of a law when it encroaches on another legislative list
questions.e: The doctrine of pith and substance is applied to determine the validity of a law that encroaches upon another sphere by looking at its true nature and character as an organic whole .

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Eclipse' is based on the principle that:
o: A pre-constitutional law inconsistent with fundamental rights is not void but remains dormant
questions.e: The doctrine of eclipse is based on the notion that a pre-constitutional law inconsistent with a fundamental right is overshadowed or eclipsed by that right and remains dormant but not dead.

questions.q: Which Article directs the Union to promote the spread and development of the Hindi language?
questions.e: Article 351 imposes a duty upon the Centre to promote the spread and development of the Hindi language so that it may become the lingua franca of India.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment act provided that the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall not be less than 12?
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 provided that the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, but the number shall not be less than 12.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment Act, what is the maximum limit for the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Central Council of Ministers?
o: 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
10 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
20 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 specifies that the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15 per cent of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: The provision of the Tenth Schedule pertaining to exemption from disqualification in case of a 'split' by one-third members of the legislature party was deleted by which amendment?
questions.e: The 91st Amendment Act of 2003 deleted the provision of the Tenth Schedule that protected defectors in case of a split by one-third of the members, meaning defectors no longer have protection on grounds of splits.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the special provision for the state of Nagaland?
questions.e: Article 371-A makes special provisions for the state of Nagaland, including matters related to Naga customary law and the special responsibility of the Governor for law and order.

questions.q: Under Article 371-D, the President is empowered to provide for equitable opportunities in public employment and education for which state?
questions.e: Article 371-D contains special provisions for Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana) to provide equitable opportunities and facilities for people belonging to different parts of the state in public employment and education.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the establishment of a Central University in the state of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.e: Article 371-E empowers the Parliament to provide for the establishment of a Central University in the state of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.q: The special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region (now Kalyana-Karnataka) are mentioned under which Article?
questions.e: Article 371-J, inserted by the 98th Amendment Act of 2012, provides special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, including the establishment of a separate development board.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment gave the right to form co-operative societies as a fundamental right?
questions.e: The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 made the right to form co-operative societies a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(c).

questions.q: Article 43-B, which requires the state to promote voluntary formation and professional management of co-operative societies, is a:
questions.e: The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 included a new Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 43-B) on the promotion of co-operative societies.

questions.q: According to the 97th Amendment Act, the accounts of every co-operative society shall be audited within how many months of the close of the financial year?
questions.e: Under Part IX-B, the accounts of every co-operative society must be audited within six months of the close of the financial year.

questions.q: Which type of party system exists in the USA and Britain?
questions.e: Modern democratic states have different kinds of party systems; USA and Britain are examples of the two-party system where two major parties exist.

questions.q: Which political analyst coined the term 'Congress system' to describe the Indian party system?
questions.e: Rajni Kothari preferred to call the Indian party system the 'one party dominance system' or the 'Congress system' due to the long period of Congress dominance.

questions.q: To be recognized as a national party, a political party must be recognized as a state party in at least how many states?
questions.e: One of the conditions for recognition as a national party is that the party must be recognized as a state party in four states.

questions.q: A party can be recognized as a state party if it secures what percentage of the total valid votes polled in the state at a general election to the Lok Sabha or State Assembly?
questions.e: According to the current conditions, a party is recognized as a state party if it secures eight per cent of the total valid votes polled in the state at a general election to the Lok Sabha or the legislative assembly.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Indian party system?
questions.e: The Indian party system is characterized by a multi-party system, one-party dominance (historically), lack of clear ideology, personality cults, and the emergence of regional parties.

questions.q: The 'Connect Central Asia' Policy of India (2012) primarily focuses on which of the following regions?
o: Eurasian countries including Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan
questions.e: India launched the 'Connect Central Asia' policy in 2012 to strengthen relations with Central Asian countries like Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.

questions.q: India's 'Act East Policy' (2014) is an upgrade of which previous policy?
questions.e: In 2014, the Modi Government upgraded India's 'Look East Policy' (initiated in 1992) and renamed it as the 'Act East Policy'.

questions.q: Which doctrine propounds that India should extend unilateral concessions to its smaller neighbors without asking for reciprocity?
questions.e: The Gujral Doctrine, propounded in 1996, advocates that India should extend unilateral concessions to smaller neighbors like Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal on the basis of non-reciprocity.

questions.q: How many principles are included in the 'Panchsheel' agreement signed in 1954?
questions.e: Panchsheel implies the five principles of conduct in international relations, embodied in the 1954 Indo-China Treaty on Tibet.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for providing inputs for decision making to the Nuclear Command Authority and executing its directives?
questions.e: The Nuclear Command Authority comprises a Political Council (chaired by the PM) and an Executive Council (chaired by the NSA). The Executive Council provides inputs and executes directives.

questions.q: The 'rarest of rare cases' doctrine for death penalty was laid down in which Supreme Court case?
questions.e: In the Bachan Singh case (1980), the Supreme Court ruled that the death penalty must be confined to the 'rarest of rare cases' .

questions.q: Which Supreme Court case established the 'collegium system' for the appointment of judges?
o: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association case (Second Judges case)
questions.e: In the Second Judges case (1993), the Supreme Court overruled its earlier judgment and formulated the procedure for appointment known as the 'collegium system' .

questions.q: The 'Jain Hawala case' is associated with which Supreme Court judgment?
o: Vineet Narain vs. Union of India
Shreya Singhal vs. Union of India
Lily Thomas vs. Union of India
questions.e: The Vineet Narain vs. Union of India (1997) case is popularly known as the Jain Hawala case and dealt with the autonomy and efficient functioning of the CBI .

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court declare that the right to fly the national flag freely is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a)?
questions.e: In the Naveen Jindal case (2004), the Supreme Court held that the right to fly the national flag freely with respect and dignity is a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(a) .

questions.q: Which 2017 judgment declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right?
questions.e: In the Justice K.S. Puttaswamy case (2017), the Supreme Court declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right protected under Article 21 .

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Basic Structure' was used to strike down Clause (4) of Article 329A in which case?
questions.e: In the Indira Nehru Gandhi case (1975), the Supreme Court reaffirmed the doctrine of basic structure and struck down clause (4) of Article 329A which had removed election disputes involving the PM from judicial jurisdiction .

questions.q: Which doctrine states that if a law is inconsistent with fundamental rights, only the offending portion is declared void, provided it can be separated?
questions.e: The doctrine of severability means that if the offending provision of a law can be separated from the constitutional portion, then only that part is declared void .

questions.q: Which doctrine is based on the maxim "what you cannot do directly, you cannot do indirectly"?
questions.e: The doctrine of colourable legislation is based on the maxim "you cannot do indirectly, what you cannot do directly," used when a legislature seeks to transgress its constitutional power covertly .

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Territorial Nexus' is primarily related to which Article?
questions.e: The doctrine of territorial nexus is related to Article 245, which deals with the extent of laws made by the Parliament and state legislatures .

questions.q: Which case ruled that the enforcement of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 cannot be suspended even during an emergency?
questions.e: While the A.D.M. Jabalpur case (1976) took a restrictive view, the 44th Amendment Act (1978) eventually ensured that Article 21 cannot be suspended, making the Jabalpur judgment academic .

questions.q: Which body was set up in 2000 to examine the working of the Constitution over the past fifty years?
o: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC)
questions.e: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC) was set up in 2000, headed by M.N. Venkatachaliah.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT an area identified for study by the NCRWC?
o: Abolition of the Office of the President
questions.e: The NCRWC identified 11 areas of study, including Union-State relations, Fundamental Rights, and Electoral reforms, but not the abolition of the Office of the President.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the total number of ministers should be fixed at a maximum of what percentage of the popular House?
questions.e: The NCRWC recommended that a ceiling on the number of ministers in a state or the Union Government be fixed at a maximum of 10% of the total strength of the popular House.

questions.q: Which committee recommended the operationalization of Fundamental Duties?
questions.e: The NCRWC recommended the early implementation of the Justice Verma Committee's recommendations on the operationalization of Fundamental Duties.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the Governor of a state should be appointed only after consultation with:
o: The Chief Minister of that state
questions.e: One of the recommendations of the NCRWC was that the President should appoint the Governor of a state only after consultation with the Chief Minister of that state.

questions.q: According to the NCRWC, a motion of no-confidence must be accompanied by:
o: A proposal of an alternative leader
questions.e: The NCRWC recommended a 'system of constructive vote of no confidence', where a motion of no-confidence against a PM must be accompanied by a proposal of an alternative leader.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the Parliament and state legislatures to regulate recruitment and conditions of service of public servants?
questions.e: Article 309 empowers the Parliament and state legislatures to regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the Union or a state.

questions.q: Under the 'Doctrine of Pleasure' (Article 310), who holds office during the pleasure of the Governor?
o: Members of the civil services of a state
questions.e: According to Article 310, members of the civil services of a state or persons holding civil posts under a state hold office during the pleasure of the Governor.

questions.q: What is the maximum duration for which a board of a co-operative society can be suspended according to the 97th Amendment Act?
questions.e: Under Part IX-B of the Constitution, no board shall be superseded or kept under suspension for a period exceeding six months.

questions.q: The 'Indra Sawhney case' (1992) upheld what percentage of reservation for OBCs in government jobs?
questions.e: In the Indra Sawhney case (1992), the Supreme Court upheld the validity of the executive order providing 27% reservation of jobs for OBCs .

questions.q: Which landmark judgment struck down Section 497 of the IPC, thereby decriminalizing adultery?
questions.e: In the Joseph Shine case (2018), the Supreme Court struck down Section 497 of the IPC, declaring that adultery is no longer a criminal offence .

questions.q: The 'Vishaka Guidelines' were replaced by which legislative act in 2013?
o: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act
questions.e: The Vishaka Guidelines (1997) filled a vacuum until the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 was enacted .

questions.q: Which doctrine allows the state to apply a law to an object not physically located in its territory if there is a sufficient connection?
questions.e: The doctrine of territorial nexus allows state laws to be valid if there is a sufficient connection (nexus) between the state and the subject matter .

questions.q: In the 'Common Cause case' (1999), the Supreme Court rejected which rule?
questions.e: In the Common Cause case (1999), the Supreme Court examined and rejected the sovereign immunity rule, stating it was outmoded.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the 'Doctrine of Precedent'?
questions.e: Article 141 incorporates the doctrine of precedent, stating that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts in India .

questions.q: The 105th Amendment Act (2021) empowered which authority to maintain a list of socially and educationally backward classes for its own purposes?
questions.e: The 105th Amendment Act of 2021 empowered states and union territories to prepare and maintain their own lists of socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.q: Which Article prohibits the interference by courts in electoral matters, specifically delimitation of constituencies?
questions.e: Article 329 bars the interference by courts in electoral matters, including the validity of laws relating to the delimitation of constituencies.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Second Law Commission of independent India?
questions.e: As per Table 70.2, the Second Law Commission (1958-1961) was headed by Justice T.V. Venkatarama Aiyar.

questions.q: The 'Sons of the soil theory' is a manifestation of which obstacle to national integration?
questions.e: 'Sons of the soil theory', which advocates preference to local people in jobs, is a form of regionalism.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the appointment of a special officer for linguistic minorities?
questions.e: Article 350B provides that the President should appoint a special officer for linguistic minorities to investigate matters relating to constitutional safeguards.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a separate general electoral roll for every territorial constituency?
questions.e: Article 325 provides that there is to be only one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency for election to the Parliament and the state legislatures.

questions.q: The 61st Amendment Act, which reduced the voting age to 18 years, came into force on which date?
questions.e: The 61st Amendment Act of 1988, which reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years, came into force on March 28, 1989.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the conduct of elections in a specific Parliamentary or assembly constituency?
questions.e: The Returning Officer (RO) of a Parliamentary or assembly constituency is responsible for the conduct of elections in that specific constituency.

questions.q: Which type of observers are deployed by the Election Commission to observe poll day proceedings at critical or vulnerable polling stations?
questions.e: Micro Observers are chosen from Central Government/PSU officials to observe poll proceedings on poll day specifically in critical or vulnerable polling stations.

questions.q: A candidate must make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before which authorized officer?
o: The Returning Officer or Assistant Returning Officer
questions.e: A candidate is required to make an oath or affirmation before an officer authorized by the Election Commission, principally the Returning Officer or Assistant Returning Officer for the constituency.

questions.q: The official election campaign period ends how many hours before polling closes?
questions.e: The official election campaign lasts at least two weeks from the drawing up of the list of nominated candidates and officially ends 48 hours before polling closes.

questions.q: Which state was the first to use Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) for the entire state during an assembly election?
questions.e: The EVMs were used for the first time in the general elections of an entire state during the Assembly elections of Goa in 1999.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of voters that a single polling station is typically expected to deal with?
questions.e: Officials try to ensure there is a polling station within two kilometres of every voter and that no polling station should have to deal with more than 1200 voters.

questions.q: Results of exit polls can only be published:
o: Immediately after a voter casts their vote
Half an hour after the end of polling hours on the last day of poll
After the final counting is completed
questions.e: The results of exit polls can only be published after half an hour of the end of polling hours on the last day of poll.

questions.q: The 'first-past-the-post' electoral system is used for elections to which body?
questions.e: Elections to the Lok Sabha are carried out using a first-past-the-post electoral system where the winner is the candidate who gets the maximum votes.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the bar to interference by courts in electoral matters?
questions.e: Article 329 of the Constitution provides for a bar to interference by courts in electoral matters, specifically regarding the validity of laws relating to delimitation or allotment of seats.

questions.q: The Delimitation Act, 2002 was enacted to set up a commission for delimitation on the basis of which census?
questions.e: The Delimitation Act, 2002 was enacted to set up a Delimitation Commission for the purpose of effecting delimitation on the basis of the 2001 census.

questions.q: Which Act regulates matters connected with the election of the President and Vice-President of India?
questions.e: The Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 regulates matters relating to or connected with elections to the offices of the President and Vice-President.

questions.q: The 'Dinesh Goswami Committee' (1990) was appointed to study which subject?
questions.e: In 1990, the National Front Government appointed a committee on electoral reforms under the chairmanship of Dinesh Goswami.

questions.q: Elector's Photo Identity Cards (EPICs) were decided to be issued by the Election Commission in which year?
questions.e: A decision was taken by the Election Commission in 1993 to issue photo identity cards (EPICs) to electors throughout the country to check bogus voting.

questions.q: According to the 1996 reforms, how many proposers are required for the nomination of a candidate sponsored by a recognized political party?
questions.e: In the case of a candidate sponsored by a recognized political party, only one proposer is required for nomination.

questions.q: If a contesting candidate belonging to a recognized political party dies before the poll, what happens to the election?
o: The election is not countermanded, but the party can propose another candidate within seven days.
The party is disqualified from the constituency.
questions.e: Under current rules, an election is not countermanded on the death of a candidate; if the deceased belonged to a recognized party, that party is given seven days to propose another candidate.

questions.q: The minimum gap between the last date for withdrawal of candidature and the polling date was reduced from 20 days to:
questions.e: One of the 1996 electoral reforms reduced the minimum gap between the last date for withdrawal of candidature and the polling date from 20 to 14 days.

questions.q: In 1997, the number of proposers and seconders for contesting the election to the office of the President was increased to:
questions.e: In 1997, the number of electors as proposers and seconders for the office of the President was increased from 10 to 50.

questions.q: What is the security deposit for a general candidate contesting elections to the Lok Sabha since 2009?
questions.e: In 2009, the amount of security deposit for general candidates contesting Lok Sabha elections was increased to ₹25,000.

questions.q: Voting rights for citizens of India living abroad (NRIs) were provided in which year?
questions.e: In 2010, a provision was made to confer voting rights to citizens of India residing outside India who have not acquired citizenship of any other country.

questions.q: Which state was the first to use VVPAT in a bye-election in 2013?
questions.e: Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) was first used in the bye-election to the Noksen Assembly Constituency of Nagaland held in 2013.

questions.q: The Supreme Court judgment in 'Lily Thomas vs. Union of India' (2013) related to:
o: Immediate disqualification of convicted MPs and MLAs
questions.e: In the Lily Thomas case (2013), the Supreme Court held that convicted Members of Parliament and MLAs will be immediately disqualified from holding membership.

questions.q: Which scheme, aimed at bringing transparency in political funding, was notified by the government in 2018?
questions.e: In 2018, the central government notified the Electoral Bond Scheme as an alternative to cash donations to bring transparency to political funding.

questions.q: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 specified how many qualifying dates in a calendar year for the preparation of electoral rolls?
questions.e: The 2021 Amendment specified the 1st January, 1st April, 1st July, and 1st October as qualifying dates for electoral roll revision.

questions.q: The term 'Coalition' is derived from which Latin word?
questions.e: The term 'coalition' is derived from the Latin word 'coalitio', which means 'to grow together'.

questions.q: Who was the Prime Minister of the first coalition government formed at the Centre in 1977?
questions.e: The first coalition government at the Centre was the Janata Party government (1977-1979), headed by Prime Minister Morarji Desai.

questions.q: Which coalition government was headed by Dr. Manmohan Singh from 2004 to 2014?
questions.e: Dr. Manmohan Singh headed the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) and UPA-II from 2004 to 2014.

questions.q: A 'Jumbo Ministry' refers to:
o: A ministry with a very large number of ministers
A ministry headed by a coalition
A ministry with only senior leaders
A ministry that lasts for five years
questions.e: The A.B. Vajpayee ministry of 1999, which had 70-plus ministers, was referred to as a 'Jumbo Ministry' due to its large size.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment act introduced the Tenth Schedule to prevent political defections?
questions.e: The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 added the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution to provide for disqualification of members on the ground of defection.

questions.q: Under the Anti-Defection Law, a member is disqualified if they vote contrary to party directions and the act is not condoned within how many days?
questions.e: A member is disqualified if they vote or abstain contrary to party direction without prior permission, provided the act is not condoned by the party within 15 days.

questions.q: In which 1992 case did the Supreme Court rule that the Presiding Officer's decision on defection is subject to judicial review?
questions.e: In the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992), the Supreme Court declared that the presiding officer functions as a tribunal and their decision is subject to judicial review.

questions.q: According to the 91st Amendment Act, a member disqualified under the Tenth Schedule is also disqualified from:
questions.e: A member of either House who is disqualified on the ground of defection shall also be disqualified to be appointed as a minister.

questions.q: Which technique used by pressure groups involves trying to place favorable persons in public office?
questions.e: According to Odegard, electioneering is the technique where pressure groups try to place persons favorably disposed toward their interests in public office.

questions.q: The oldest and largest agrarian pressure group in India is:
questions.e: The All India Kisan Sabha is described as the oldest and the largest agrarian group in India.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an 'Anomic' pressure group in India?
questions.e: Anomic pressure groups involve spontaneous breakthroughs like riots or demonstrations; examples include Naxalite Groups and the ULFA.

questions.q: The National Integration Council (NIC) was first constituted in which year?
questions.e: The National Integration Council (NIC) was constituted in 1961 following the National Integration Conference.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of the National Integration Council?
questions.e: The National Integration Council consists of the Prime Minister as its Chairman.

questions.q: Which autonomous body was set up in 1992 under the Union Home Ministry to promote communal harmony?
questions.e: The National Foundation for Communal Harmony (NFCH) was set up in 1992 as an autonomous body under the Union Home Ministry.

questions.q: India's foreign policy principle of 'Panchsheel' was signed with which country?
questions.e: Panchsheel was embodied in the Indo-China Treaty on Tibet, signed in 1954 by Jawaharlal Nehru and Chou-En-Lai.

questions.q: In which year did India host the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM)?
questions.e: India has been an active member of the Commonwealth and hosted the CHOGM at New Delhi in 1983.

questions.q: Which Indian was elected as the President of the UN General Assembly in 1953?
questions.e: In 1953, Vijay Lakshmi Pandit of India was elected as the President of the UN General Assembly.

questions.q: India maintains a "No First Use" posture regarding which type of weapons?
questions.e: India's nuclear doctrine includes a posture of "No First Use," meaning nuclear weapons will only be used in retaliation against a nuclear attack.

questions.q: The "Look East Policy" was first initiated in 1992 by which Prime Minister?
questions.e: The "Look East Policy" was first initiated in 1992 by the then Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.

questions.q: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC) submitted its report in:
questions.e: The NCRWC was set up in 2000 and submitted its final report in 2002.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the NCRWC?
questions.e: The NCRWC was an 11-member Commission headed by M.N. Venkatachaliah, the former Chief Justice of India.

questions.q: The NCRWC recommended that the minimum number of days for sittings of the Lok Sabha should be fixed at:
questions.e: The Commission recommended that the minimum number of days for sittings of the Lok Sabha should be fixed at 120 days.

questions.q: In the 'Kesavananda Bharati case' (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament can amend the Constitution EXCEPT for its:
questions.e: In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the court held that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution but cannot destroy its 'basic structure'.

questions.q: Which judgment established that 'Secularism' is a part of the basic structure of the Constitution?
questions.e: In the S.R. Bommai case (1994), the court laid down that secularism is a part of the basic structure of the constitution.

questions.q: The 'Doctrine of Severability' is based on which Article of the Constitution?
questions.e: Article 13 is the basis of the doctrine of severability, used to resolve the validity of laws declared unconstitutional.
